Write a set's shard table

Source: R/level.R
a5_write_pyramid_set_table.Rd

Writes the index of a set whose shards were written one at a time, with a5_write_pyramid_level() or by another writer, as a Parquet table: one row per shard, the set's own fields in its footer (format version 4). A reader filters the rows by tier and box with row-group statistics, and the table can carry columns of its writer's beside the format's, such as a year or a build name, so a store's manifest can be its set's index. A shard may be listed with no file, as empty.

Usage

a5_write_pyramid_set_table(
  shards,
  dest,
  template,
  tiers,
  metadata = NULL,
  compression = c("snappy", "zstd", "none")
)

Arguments

shards

A data frame with one row per shard, by tier and then cell: tier (from 0), cell (an a5R::a5_cell at the tier's shard resolution), path (the file, relative to the set's directory with / separators; NA for an empty shard), rows, tiles, bytes, footer_bytes and xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax (the box of every tile, xmax above 180 across the antimeridian, as a5_pyramid_info() gives it; NA for an empty shard). a5_pyramid_info() gives a file's values. Any other columns are written after these.

dest

Path of the table to write, usually set.parquet in the set's directory.

template

Path of one of the shards: the set's columns, weights, leaves' resolution and a5 crate are taken from its index.

tiers

A data frame of the tiers, as for a5_write_pyramid_set().

metadata

Named character vector of the set's metadata.

compression

"snappy" (default), "zstd" or "none". hyparquet decodes snappy itself; zstd needs the hyparquet-compressors package in the browser.

Value

dest, invisibly.

See also

a5_pyramid_set_info() reads it back.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)
key <- a5_cell_to_supercell(cells[1], resolution = 9)
a5_write_pyramid_level(data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells))),
                       file.path(dir, "leaves.parquet"), value,
                       shard = list(tier = 0, cell = key, resolution = 9))
info <- a5_pyramid_info(file.path(dir, "leaves.parquet"))
shards <- data.frame(
  tier = 0L, path = "leaves.parquet", rows = sum(info$tiles$rows),
  tiles = nrow(info$tiles), bytes = info$bytes, footer_bytes = info$footer_bytes,
  xmin = info$bbox[["xmin"]], ymin = info$bbox[["ymin"]],
  xmax = info$bbox[["xmax"]], ymax = info$bbox[["ymax"]]
)
shards$cell <- key
tiers <- data.frame(lod_min = 15, lod_max = 15, shard_resolution = 9)
a5_write_pyramid_set_table(shards, file.path(dir, "set.parquet"),
                           template = file.path(dir, "leaves.parquet"), tiers = tiers)
a5_pyramid_set_info(dir)$shards
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>    tier cell             path    rows tiles bytes footer_bytes  xmin  ymin  xmax
#>   <int> <a5_cell>        <chr>  <dbl> <int> <dbl>        <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     0 63bb920000000000 leave…  1024     1  6311          638 -3.22  55.9 -3.13
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: ymax <dbl>
